meta.scope: School revision list for the A Level November test on 26/11/2026, Grammar: Present Simple p. 10-13, Present Continuous p. 14-16, If Conditional Type 0 p. 26, Type 1 p. 27, Stative Verbs p. 28, Will + Be Going to p. 31

reasons.ps_s: With a singular subject, add "s", "es" or "ies" to the verb. (Book p. 10)
reasons.ps_pl: With a plural subject, "I" or "you", use the verb with no "s". (Book p. 10)
reasons.ps_be: "be" in the present simple is am, is or are. (Book p. 10)
reasons.ps_have: "have" in the present simple is have or has. (Book p. 10)
reasons.ps_time: Time words like "always", "usually" and "every" go with the present simple. (Book p. 10)
reasons.neg_does: With a singular subject, use does + not + verb, with no "s" on the verb. (Book p. 12)
reasons.neg_do: With a plural subject, "I" or "you", use do + not + verb. (Book p. 12)
reasons.neg_be: "be" does not need a helping verb: isn't, aren't, I'm not. (Book p. 12)
reasons.q_does: With a singular subject, use does + subject + verb, with no "s" on the verb. (Book p. 13)
reasons.q_do: With a plural subject, "I" or "you", use do + subject + verb. (Book p. 13)
reasons.q_be: "be" does not need a helping verb: Am I? Is he? Are they? (Book p. 13)
reasons.pc: The present continuous is am, is or are + verb + ing. (Book p. 14)
reasons.pc_time: Time words like "now", "at the moment" and "this week" go with the present continuous. (Book p. 14)
reasons.c0: Type 0 is If + present simple, present simple. (Book p. 26)
reasons.c1: Type 1 is If + present simple, will + infinitive. (Book p. 27)
reasons.c1_comma: When the sentence starts with the result clause, do not add a comma. (Book p. 27)
reasons.st: Stative verbs such as think, love, have, be, believe, see, hear and smell are not used in the continuous form. (Book p. 28)
reasons.st_dyn: Some stative verbs become dynamic verbs when the meaning changes, for example "What are you thinking about?" (Book p. 28)
reasons.will: Use will for quick decisions, promises, offers and predictions. (Book p. 31)
reasons.gt: Use be going to for planned actions and for predictions based on what you can see. (Book p. 31)

learn.head: Present Simple Tense
lines: Use: habits, routines, facts and timetables.
Add "s", "es" or "ies" to the verb with a singular subject. Ex.: He plays tennis every week.
Use the verb with no "s" with a plural subject, "I" and "You". Ex.: They work hard daily.
Irregular verbs: be is am, is or are. have is have or has.
Time expressions: always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never, daily, every day.

learn.head: Negative Form
lines: do + not + verb (inf.) with a plural subject, I and you. Ex.: I don't like chocolate.
does + not + verb (inf.) with a singular subject. Ex.: She doesn't work on Fridays.
be does not need a helping verb. Ex.: She isn't responsible for doing these tasks.

learn.head: Present Continuous Tense
lines: Use: an action happening at the moment of speaking, the near future, or a changing action.
Form: am, is or are + verb + ing. Ex.: He's working at the moment.
If the verb ends with "e", cross it out. Ex.: She is smiling at us.
If the verb ends with CVC, double the last letter. Ex.: They're planning to travel to Cairo this week.
Time expressions: now, at the moment, at the present time, this week or month.

learn.head: Negative Form and Question Form
lines: Negative: am, is or are + not + verb + ing. Ex.: They aren't eating chocolate now.
Question: am, is or are + subject + verb + ing. Ex.: What is he doing at the moment?

learn.head: If Conditional: Type 0
lines: Use: for general truths and scientific facts.
Form: If + present simple, present simple. Ex.: If you heat water, it boils.
If the sentence starts with the result clause, don't add a comma between the two clauses.

learn.head: If Conditional: Type 1
lines: Use: something that can happen in the future if a certain condition is met.
Form: If + present simple, will + infinitive. Ex.: If you study hard, you will pass the exam.
If the sentence starts with the result clause, don't add a comma. Ex.: You will pass the exam if you study hard.

learn.head: Lesson 1: Stative Verbs
lines: Dynamic verbs show activities. Ex.: drive, watch, listen.
Stative verbs express a state, not an action: thoughts, emotions, ownership, beliefs and senses. Ex.: think, love, dislike, have, own, be, believe, see, hear, smell.
These verbs are not used in the continuous form.
Some stative verbs become dynamic when the meaning changes. Ex.: I think it's a good idea. (opinion) What are you thinking about? (action)
Ex.: Sam is a very foolish person. (his character) Sam is being foolish. (how he is acting)

learn.head: Stative or dynamic?
lines: Stative verbs are not used in the continuous form. Ex.: I think it's a good idea.
The same verb can be dynamic with a different meaning. Ex.: What are you thinking about?
Exercise C: each verb is used once as a stative verb and once as a dynamic verb. (Book p. 29)

parts.title: Will and be going to
parts.dir: A. Fill in the blanks using will or be going to.

learn.head: Lesson 2: Will & Be Going To
lines: Will + inf.: quick (spontaneous) decisions. Ex.: It's raining! I will get an umbrella.
Will + inf.: promises, offers or threats. Ex.: I will call you when I arrive.
Will + inf.: predictions and formal statements. Ex.: I'm sure you will love this movie.
Be going to + inf.: planned future actions. Ex.: I'm going to study medicine at university.
Be going to + inf.: predictions based on evidence. Ex.: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.

items.parent: The school's model answer says "will". The book's rule on p. 31 says a prediction based on evidence uses "be going to", and "It's very late" can be read as evidence. Ask the teacher which answer the test expects.
